focus: security: arm-event identity, killer spawn failure, and re-arm behavior across runtimes

findingDetails.title: killer spawn errors leave interactive runtimes armed without a retry trigger

traceabilityChecks.spec_code: phase 016 asks whether automatic handover fires every time and requires confirmed P1 fixes
traceabilityChecks.agent_cross_runtime: all five adapters checked; four interactive event flows reviewed for stalled-hop consequence

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: The finding crosses adapter spawn handling, killer signaling, and the wrapper's post-exit decision.

targetSelection.selectionReason: Trace each arm adapter through spawn failure handling, re-arm eligibility, killer signaling, and the wrapper's relaunch gate.
omittedHighRiskTargets: hook registration, shim path, and full Hermes exit timing are deferred to later steered iterations

searchLedger.hypothesis: An adapter may arm a record belonging to another loop, session, or runtime, or accept an unrelated event.
searchLedger.invariant: Only the matching loop/session/runtime and intended host event may arm this record.

searchActions.result: The shared guard checks loopId, sessionId, runtime, status, and live-killer ownership; Codex and Hermes match named events, while Pi and OpenCode enter through their host event handlers.

searchLedger.rationale: The shared identity gate refuses mismatched loop/session/runtime and adapter handlers are bound to their host event; Claude registration itself is deferred for direct config verification.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: No mismatched record was found in the reviewed event paths.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A repeated arm event may spawn a redundant killer for a record that already has a live killer.
searchLedger.invariant: An already-armed record may be re-armed only after its killer lock is gone.

searchActions.result: armableRecord rejects non-pending status while the live killer lock exists; the archived Claude omission is fixed by the current shared guard.

searchLedger.rationale: Current shared guard checks status plus liveKillerPid before re-arming.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: The current code rejects an already-armed record while a killer owns the lock.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A first killer spawn error may leave the runtime alive with an armed record and no supervisor to signal it.
searchLedger.invariant: A failed killer launch must not leave an interactive automatic hop waiting indefinitely for the runtime to exit.

searchActions.queryOrPath: four interactive arm handlers and killer startup
searchActions.result: Each logs spawn failure but leaves the record armed; no immediate retry is scheduled.
Only the detached killer waits then signals; the shell wrapper waits for runtime exit before it evaluates the armed record.

searchActions.queryOrPath: adapter spawn-error tests and archived review reports
searchActions.result: Current tests assert the armed record remains on spawn errors. Prior reports only cover duplicate Claude arm and other killer concerns, not retry after initial spawn failure.

searchLedger.rationale: A one-time spawn error has no self-retry, and the wrapper cannot evaluate the armed record until the interactive runtime has exited.

searchLedger.hypothesis: Re-arming after a dead killer may preserve an old timestamp or cwd, causing the wrapper to reject the replacement killer's record.
searchLedger.invariant: A replacement killer must supervise a record with a fresh armedAt and current cwd.

searchActions.result: arm restamps armedAt and cwd, and the core test asserts both persisted values change on re-arm.
Pi adapter test confirms an old armed record is re-armed with live cwd so the wrapper will relaunch.

searchLedger.rationale: The shared transition restamps both fields, and current tests cover the core behavior plus a runtime adapter.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: The stale timestamp/cwd failure fixed in phase 011 does not remain in current arm logic.
